reads.sell: A lean, steely Chardonnay from the cool north of Burgundy, with green apple, lemon and a chalky, oyster shell edge. It is bright and dry, and it wants oysters or a simply grilled fish.

why.grape: No loud grape aroma of its own: the wine reads as winemaking, lees and chalk on a medium bodied frame, which is the shape shifting tell of Chardonnay.
why.climate: Tart green apple and citrus, high acidity and moderate alcohol say a cool site.

reads.sell: A fuller white Burgundy from the Côte de Beaune, nutty and structured, with yellow apple and peach wrapped in cream, hazelnut and a little toast from new oak. It is dry and medium to full bodied, a wine for roast chicken or a butter sauce.

why.grape: Butter and cream from malolactic conversion, hazelnut lees and toasty new oak on a medium to full body point to Chardonnay in the Burgundian cellar style.
why.climate: Riper yellow fruit, medium plus alcohol and acidity that has eased from high read as a moderate climate.
